name: Killer 1v1: Killer Meets Killer, Never An Old App
note: KP-10 / KP-14 (2026-11-06). A killer search has its own queue (/queue_killer) because the /queue rule refuses any field it does not name and an app up to 33 would host a standard room for a killer ticket. Each 'ignored' in the gate is paired with the same message being taken by a search of its own kind.

mutations.name: a killer search waits in the standard queue
mutations.why: An app up to 33 reads /queue, takes the killer ticket and hosts a standard room: the killer player is dropped onto a standard board.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer ticket waits in the killer queue

mutations.name: the broadcast ticket does not say killer
mutations.why: Two killer searchers that both saw an empty queue meet only through the broadcast; unmarked, each takes the other's ticket as a standard one and ignores it.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer search must say so in its broadcast ticket

mutations.name: a ticket of the other kind is not skipped
mutations.why: The killer search withdraws and re-posts its own ticket for every old ticket it hears — a moment in which another killer searcher finds an empty queue — and re-broadcasts each time.
mutations.find: if (ticketKind(data) !== (service.searchingKind || 'classic')) return;   // a search of the other kind (KP-10)
mutations.expectFailure: a ticket it could never take made it withdraw and re-post its own

mutations.name: a board of the other kind is adopted
mutations.why: A killer search ends on a standard board, or an app gets a killer board it is not searching for.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer search adopted a standard board

mutations.name: the host that found a queued ticket deals a standard board
mutations.why: The host sits in a standard room while the waiting killer player refuses the board and keeps searching: one player in a match, the other in the lobby.

mutations.name: the room keeps no cages
mutations.why: The room says killer but has no cages: the game starts as a sparse standard board nobody can solve by sight.
mutations.expectFailure: the room's cages do not cover the board once

mutations.name: a refused killer ticket is taken as queued
mutations.why: Before the /queue_killer rules are published every killer search is refused; the lobby would wait twelve seconds and then say nobody came.
mutations.expectFailure: a refused killer ticket must report "could not connect"

mutations.name: Firebase answers true for a refused write
mutations.why: The local transport's switch would pass while the real server's refusal is swallowed: on a phone the killer search waits for nobody.
mutations.find:
console.warn('[FirebaseTransport] enqueue failed:', e?.message || e);
      return false;
mutations.replace:
console.warn('[FirebaseTransport] enqueue failed:', e?.message || e);
      return true;
mutations.expectFailure: a write the server refuses must answer false

mutations.name: Firebase writes killer tickets to /queue
mutations.why: The same old-app collision as the local queue, on the only transport phones use.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer ticket must go to /queue_killer

mutations.name: a rematch deals a standard board
mutations.why: A killer pair asks for a rematch and gets standard — and the requester, whose room is killer, refuses the board, so the two sides never start the same match.

mutations.name: a rematch keeps the old cages
mutations.why: The new board is played inside the previous match's cages, whose sums no longer add up: an unsolvable rematch.
mutations.expectFailure: a cage sum is not its cells' sum in the solution

mutations.name: a rematch board of the other kind is taken
mutations.why: The opponent's acceptance can change the match's kind under the player.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer room took a standard board as its rematch

mutations.name: a cage may repeat a digit
mutations.why: A peer could send cages that agree with the sums but not with the rules; the board has no answer by killer rules.
mutations.expectFailure: a cage with a digit twice is refused

mutations.name: a cage sum is not checked against the solution
mutations.why: A peer could send cages whose sums contradict its own answer: the board looks fine and cannot be finished.
mutations.find: || ds.reduce((s, d) => s + d, 0) !== cage.sum) return false;
mutations.expectFailure: a cage sum that is not its cells' sum is refused

mutations.name: the replay is saved without its cages
mutations.why: A killer replay shows a board with too few digits to follow (KP-14).

mutations.name: a stored replay keeps a torn cage set
mutations.why: A damaged record would be drawn with cages missing over part of the board.
mutations.expectFailure: a torn cage set is dropped

mutations.name: the lobby searches for standard whatever is chosen
mutations.why: The killer switch shows in the 1v1 lobby and does nothing.
mutations.expectFailure: the lobby must search for the chosen kind

mutations.name: the hook drops the kind
mutations.why: The lobby asks for killer and the service searches standard.
